items.q: What is quick commerce and which platforms matter in India?
a: Quick commerce (q-commerce) is the delivery of groceries, FMCG, beauty and everyday products in roughly 10–30 minutes from local dark stores. In India the platforms that matter are Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket (BB Now).
gaa-tha onboards brands onto all of them and runs the catalogue, availability, ads and ratings as one operation.

items.q: What does a quick commerce agency do?
a: A quick commerce agency gets a brand listed on 10-minute delivery platforms and then runs the account: catalogue and thumbnails, city and dark-store availability, purchase orders and replenishment, promotions and ads, ratings and monthly reporting.
We do this for Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket from one team, with one monthly report.

items.q: Which quick commerce platform should I launch on first?
a: Start where your category and your target cities overlap best. Blinkit and Zepto lead metro grocery and FMCG; Swiggy Instamart is strong on food and impulse categories; BigBasket suits staples and larger packs; Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now are expanding city by city.
We map your SKUs, margins and cities against each platform's category demand and recommend an order before you apply anywhere.

items.q: How long does Blinkit, Zepto or Instamart onboarding take?
a: Typically two to six weeks from application to first purchase order, depending on category approvals, documentation and how quickly catalogue and images are ready. Food and beauty categories with licence checks take longer than packaged non-food.
We prepare the documents, catalogue and images in parallel so the platform review is the only wait.

items.q: What documents do I need to sell on Blinkit or Zepto?
a: Usually GST registration, brand ownership proof or a brand authorisation letter, bank account details, a trademark certificate or application where available, and category licences such as FSSAI for food. Product data — barcodes, MRP, pack sizes, shelf life, dimensions — is needed for the catalogue.
Requirements change by platform and category, so we share a current checklist before you apply.

items.q: Are there fees to get listed on quick commerce platforms?
a: Platforms work on a margin per SKU and may have onboarding, listing or marketing contributions; these vary by category and change over time, and some are negotiable at scale.
We share the current structure for your category before you sign and plan pack sizes and pricing so the margin works after platform costs.

items.q: What is marketplace account management?
a: Marketplace account management is the ongoing operation of a brand's seller account on platforms like Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra and Nykaa: listings and A+ content, pricing and deals, sponsored ads, inventory and fulfilment planning, account health, reviews and monthly reporting.
gaa-tha runs it as a monthly retainer with a named account manager and a P&L-style report.

items.q: Do you handle Amazon and Flipkart onboarding?
a: Yes. Seller registration, Brand Registry or brand approval, category approvals, catalogue creation, A+ content, Brand Store and a go-live checklist — then optional monthly account management.
Fashion and beauty brands can add Myntra, Nykaa and AJIO; price-led categories can add Meesho and JioMart.

items.q: Can you manage D2C, marketplaces and quick commerce together?
a: Yes — that is the point of the practice. One team handles your Shopify store, Amazon and Flipkart accounts and Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart listings, so pricing, pack sizes, content and promotions stay consistent across every channel.
You get one monthly report showing revenue and margin by channel rather than three agencies with three versions of the truth.

items.q: Do you build and manage Shopify stores?
a: Yes. We design and develop Shopify stores — custom themes and sections, checkout and payment integrations, COD and pincode rules, Meta Pixel and Conversions API, GA4 — and run monthly store management for product uploads, price changes, banners, apps and fixes.
Migrations from Amazon or WooCommerce are included in scope where needed.

items.q: Can one website serve multiple store locations or franchises?
a: Yes. A multi-location Shopify build lets the customer enter a pincode or choose an outlet; the order is routed to that outlet with a WhatsApp notification, and each outlet can have its own availability, delivery rules and prepaid/COD settings on one shared catalogue and price list.
It suits retail chains, franchises, sweet and snack stores and local delivery brands.

items.q: How do you price ecommerce and quick commerce services?
a: Onboarding is a one-time project fee per platform. Ongoing work — account management, store management, ads — is a monthly retainer scoped to the number of platforms, SKUs and cities. Ad spend is paid by you directly to the platform, with no markup.
We send a written scope and price within 48 hours of the first call.

items.q: How do you measure success on marketplaces?
a: Orders, revenue and net margin after fees and returns; advertising ACoS/TACoS; organic rank for target keywords; conversion rate; ratings and review count; and account health. On quick commerce we add availability and fill rate by city.
All of it is reported monthly against the targets agreed at the start.

items.q: My listings are live but not selling — can you fix that?
a: Usually. Stalled listings almost always have one of four problems: weak titles and images, no reviews, uncompetitive pricing, or no advertising. We audit the account, fix content and pricing, set up sponsored ads and a compliant review process, and track rank and conversion weekly.
If the problem is availability — out of stock or not live in the right cities — we fix that first.

items.q: Do you create product images and A+ content?
a: Yes. White-background packshots, lifestyle scenes, infographic 'why buy' images, pack-size visuals and A+ or enhanced-content modules, made to each platform's specs — with AI-assisted shoots for large catalogues so 200-SKU ranges do not take months.
Quick-commerce thumbnails are treated as their own format: they have to win in a two-second scroll.

items.q: Do you make cinema ads?
a: Yes. Trailer-grade 10, 20 and 30-second films cut for cinema screens, OTT, YouTube and in-store displays — produced live-action or with AI and human art direction, delivered in 2.39:1 scope and vertical versions.
They work best for retail chains, FMCG launches and festive campaigns that need city-wide recall.

items.q: Do you generate B2B and export leads for manufacturers?
a: Yes. LinkedIn outreach to named decision-makers, Meta and LinkedIn lead ads, IndiaMART and TradeIndia listing optimisation, WhatsApp first-reply templates and a lead-qualification SOP with a tracker your sales team will actually use.
It is built for manufacturers, exporters, packaging, machinery and bulk food suppliers.

items.q: Can we see results from similar brands?
a: Yes. Our case studies are published one by one as each client approves them and the numbers are confirmed from real reports — we do not publish estimates. Browse what is live on the work page, and ask us for a walkthrough of unpublished work in your category on a call.
Every case study lists the services used and links to those service pages.

items.q: Do you work with manufacturers, FMCG, retail, real estate and education brands?
a: Yes. Current and past clients include packaged-snack and FMCG brands, sweets and gifting retailers, machinery, coatings and packaging manufacturers, a co-living brand, an overseas-education consultancy and a D2C skincare brand.
The process is the same across industries; the channels and references change.

items.q: Do you work with international clients?
a: Yes. We work remotely-first with brands outside India — including a trading-card and hobbies retailer in Canada — on social content, creative, copy and websites. On-ground shoots are arranged locally where needed.
Time zones are handled with a shared calendar and weekly reviews.
